hints: Focus on the -OH group first, since an alcohol must use the -ol suffix and the chain must be numbered to give it the lowest possible number.
Trace the longest continuous carbon chain through the carbon attached to OH, you will find it is 5 carbons long with the OH on carbon 2.
Look at the branched carbon next to the OH carbon, it carries two identical methyl groups, so combine the parent name, substituents and position of the OH to complete the name.
walkthrough:
**Decode the skeletal formula**

Great start, let us redraw what each line means. Each end and bend is a carbon.

The structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-C(CH}_3)_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$. The left $\text{CH}_3$ is joined to $\text{CH(OH)}$, which is joined to a carbon with two $\text{CH}_3$ branches and a $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group.

**Find the longest parent chain**

This is the classic trap. Do not stop at 4 carbons. The longest continuous chain going through the $\text{C-OH}$ carbon is 5 carbons long.

$$\text{C1 - C2(OH) - C3 - C4 - C5}$$ That gives a pentane parent with an alcohol, so pentan-2-ol.

**Number to give OH the lowest locant and name branches**

Number from the left so OH is on C2, not from the right where it would be on C4. Carbon 3 then has two methyl groups.

$$\text{3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol}$$ This uses the -ol suffix for the principal functional group and lists both methyl substituents.

options.A: Incorrect because the parent chain is too short. It picks butane (4 carbons) instead of the longest 5-carbon pentane chain. IUPAC rule is always choose the longest continuous chain containing the functional group.
options.B: Incorrect and chemically impossible. It places the OH on C2 of a butane that already has an ethyl and a methyl on C2, which would give that carbon five bonds. It also misidentifies the parent chain and the position of the OH.
options.C: Correct. The longest chain is 5 carbons, numbered to give OH position 2, giving pentan-2-ol. Carbon 3 has two methyl substituents, so 3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol fits perfectly.
options.D: Incorrect because of two naming rule errors. An alcohol must use the -ol suffix, not the hydroxy- prefix when it is the principal group, and the chain is numbered from the wrong end. Numbering from the left gives OH position 2, which is lower than 4, so 4-hydroxy is wrong.
